reasoning: All four findings of the earlier rounds are closed: the worktree containing the cwd is excluded from the cleanup so the run never eats the plan it is about to move, the worktree listing is read once after the gate with a failure that exits 1 before any GitHub write instead of an unnamed fallback base, the fake now answers that listing the way git does, and every added spec sentence has a test that asserts it.

simpler.evidence: Simpler designs named and rejected in the artifacts: keep `-c` plus `EnterWorktree name=<change>` (D1, rejected: that tool branches from `origin/main` unlinked from the issue, so the merge would not close it — requirement "GitHub links branch, PR and issue", scenario Merge); a SessionStart hook for the cleanup (D5, rejected: a second entry point with its own install path in consumers for the same effect one step earlier); `git branch --merged` or "upstream gone" instead of `gh pr view` (D5, rejected on the observed `allow_squash_merge:true, delete_branch_on_merge:false`); git's remote-name guessing instead of the explicit `--track -b … origin/<change>` (D1); deleting the merged branch and ignoring `.claude/worktrees/` in consumers (Non-Goals). The simplest design of all — serialize the agents — is what scenario "Parallel changes" rejects. The change stays inside one script, one SKILL.md group and the tests; no new module, no new entry point, no new state on disk.

map.evidence: tasks.md:36-45 maps every scenario of the delta 1:1: Parallel changes → test_parallel_changes; Worktree step fails after the branch exists → test_worktree_step_fails_after_branch_exists; Merged change's worktree → test_merged_changes_worktree; Started from inside the previous change's worktree → test_started_from_inside_the_previous_changes_worktree; Worktree listing fails → the listing case of test_worktree_step_fails_after_branch_exists; Cleanup fails → test_cleanup_fails; Tasks of a new change → test_tasks_of_a_new_change_start plus test_planning_workflow::test_tasks_of_a_new_change; Propose run stopped before its tail → test_propose_run_stopped_before_its_tail; Merge → n/a with its reason (scenario_coverage); the five untouched scenarios of the MODIFIED requirement → their existing tests. The MODIFIED bodies remain a faithful superset of openspec/specs/implementation/spec.md:60-124, so the archive drops no requirement. Nit, not blocking: the listing case lives in a test whose name says "after the branch exists" while it asserts `_develops(gh) == []` before any branch — a `test_worktree_listing_fails` of its own would read straight, and 1.5 would name it.

red.evidence: Group 1 is RED-first: 1.1-1.4 write the tests, 1.5 runs `check_red.py` on nine node ids (test_propose_run_stopped_before_its_tail, test_tasks_of_a_new_change_start, test_parallel_changes, test_worktree_step_fails_after_branch_exists, test_interrupted_start_names_the_continuation, test_merged_changes_worktree, test_started_from_inside_the_previous_changes_worktree, test_cleanup_fails, test_planning_workflow::test_tasks_of_a_new_change) and verifies each fails in its body before the commit; Groups 2-3 then write the code. Every mapped test plus the continuation test 1.3 edits is in that list. Three of the behavioural tests run against a real repository with a real git (1.2, and both real-repository tests of 1.4 through `git_runner`), not only against the fake.

platform.evidence: Every behaviour the design rests on is observed with its output beside it: `gh issue develop -c` semantics and `git worktree add --track -b` flags (proposal Why, `--help`); `EnterWorktree` path mode and its `.claude/worktrees/` requirement (tool description); `.claude/worktrees/` already excluded (`git check-ignore -v`); the default-fetch-refspec precondition with the single-branch failure messages and exit 128 (D1:32-40, probes, git 2.45.1); the main worktree as the first `worktree` entry of `git worktree list --porcelain` from any linked worktree, forward-slash paths on Windows (D1:41-46); the squash-merge repository settings and the `gh pr view` outputs including the rc-1 `no pull requests found` (D5:88-95). Also checked by this review: `.claude` is in `ci_check.py`'s `_EXCLUDE_DIRS` and a relative `core.hooksPath` resolves per worktree, so the nested checkout has no tooling effect. The round-4 finding is closed: the listing is read once after the gate and a failure exits 1 before `gh issue develop` with no fallback base (D1:46-49, 2.1, scenario "Worktree listing fails"), and 1.1's fake now answers that listing the way git does (`worktree <root>` / `HEAD <sha>` / `branch refs/heads/main` plus `extra_worktrees`), so the unit tests exercise the first-entry rule instead of an unwritten path.

replaced.evidence: Each replaced input and dropped guard has its list beside it: `gh issue develop -c` → develop without `-c` plus fetch, worktree add and move (D1, D2), with the `left` list rebuilt in D4 and asserted by 1.3; `git switch <change>` gone from the script, the `left` list and the resume text (D4), with the continuation test updated and `EnterWorktree` taking its place (D3); `archive_change`'s dirty-tree guard keeps its meaning because the archive now runs in the change's own worktree (`ROOT = Path.cwd()`, D3) and the upstream its `git push` needs comes from `--track` (asserted by 1.2's `rev-parse --abbrev-ref @{u}`); the cleanup replaces no existing guard and adds no `git branch -d/-D` (Non-Goal, AGENTS.md). The round-3 finding stays closed (main-worktree rooting, resolved-path comparison, files still moving from the cwd) and the round-4 one is closed: the worktree containing the cwd is excluded from the scan in D5:79-82, in the spec requirement and in 2.2's `prune_merged_worktrees(main, root, listing, gh)`, so the run cannot remove the tree that holds the plan the gate read and D2 moves.

catcher.evidence: Every named catcher reaches a traceable step: the review-and-`Planned` gate exits 2 before any branch (unchanged); a failed worktree listing exits 1 before `gh issue develop`, so no branch and no Project write happen (D1:46-49, scenario "Worktree listing fails", `_develops(gh) == []`); a failure once the remote branch exists exits 1 with the `left` list starting at the failed step, before `set_status "In Progress"` and the provenance comment (D4, 1.3); a dirty or unremovable merged worktree prints `kept:` on stderr and the start goes on (D5, test_cleanup_fails, exit 0 with develop called); a half-way move is named as the step left with the source still readable (Risks); Group 4 runs `openspec validate --strict --all` and `ci_check`; the review loop after the PR is bounded with the escalation to the person in 5.3. No path now ends in silence or in deleting its own input.

length.evidence: The added requirement (specs/implementation/spec.md:4-14, ~120 words) is asserted clause by clause: the worktree path, the tracking and the untracked move by test_parallel_changes and 1.1's argv order; "SHALL NOT change the branch, the index or any other file" by 1.2's before/after `git status --porcelain` diff (only the gone `?? openspec/changes/b/` and the new `?? .claude/`); Group 0 entering the worktree by test_planning_workflow::test_tasks_of_a_new_change (`EnterWorktree`, `.claude/worktrees/`); the `left` list and the absent `git switch` by test_worktree_step_fails_after_branch_exists and test_interrupted_start_names_the_continuation; "the main worktree's `.claude/worktrees/`, other than the one containing its cwd" by test_started_from_inside_the_previous_changes_worktree (new worktree at the main worktree, nothing nested, `prev` still there and no `removed:` for it); the removal, the `kept:` lines and "not fail the start on a cleanup failure" by test_merged_changes_worktree and test_cleanup_fails. The two MODIFIED clauses are one phrase each ("without checkout", "the change's worktree"), covered by the existing tests of those requirements. Nits for the applying pass, not blocking: D5:79-82's aside about the cwd exclusion lost its main clause ("… it is left for a later start from elsewhere it asks `gh pr view …`") and reads as one run-on sentence, and proposal.md:58 does not name the fake's new `extra_worktrees` knob it now describes.

bespoke.evidence: The proposal's Impact (proposal.md:56-61) and the design add no script, check or non-test file: `start_change.py`, `SKILL.md` Group 0 and three test files are edited, and the spec change is carried by the archive. The one new function, `prune_merged_worktrees`, lives in the script it serves and uses the standard tools for its job — `git worktree list --porcelain`, `git worktree remove`, `gh pr view --json state` — instead of a marker file, a new hook (D5 rejects the SessionStart hook) or a bespoke check; the fake's `pr_states`, `git_runner` and `extra_worktrees` are test seams in the existing `delivery_fakes.Gh`. No ADR, with the reason stated. `additions` is therefore empty.
